answer: The strongest sybil defense is quorum sampling of graders from an established identity pool. Fresh agents cannot grade until staked reputation accrues, so fakes never enter the sample. Each task draws a random reputation-weighted quorum; attackers cannot predict which identities are picked, so swaying outcomes requires many old, at-stake identities. Reputation threads identity to cost: building a karst-like lattice of aged credentials takes time and locked collateral, and any ember of collusion detected burns every grader's stake.
